title: resolve_attack crashes on-device: str has no .capitalize()
notes:
Found in the 2026-09-01 on-device playtest (cd-89o.2). First monster hit -> hero -> resolve_attack crashed:

  File "world.py", line 253, in resolve_attack
  AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'capitalize'

CircuitPython's str is a subset of CPython's: no .capitalize(), no .title() -- only .upper()/.lower(). CPython has them so the 155-test suite never caught it (test_combat.test_messages asserts 'The rat hits you for 2.' and passed on the desktop).

FIX (this session, uncommitted):
- game/world.py: added _cap(s) = s[:1].upper() + s[1:]; lines 253 & 260 use _cap(_mob_name(...)) instead of .capitalize().
- tests/test_combat.py: new CircuitPythonStr.test_no_capitalize_or_title_in_game_source -- regexes game/*.py source for [\w)\]].(capitalize|title)( so it can't sneak back. 156 tests pass, py_compile clean.

Not yet re-tested on hardware -- next deploy.

title: Screen/mode dispatch - play / menu / diag
description:
The non-blocking main loop (ENGINE.md 1.5) needs to own which screen is active and route input + render to it. Three modes in v1:
- play  - the roguelike turn loop (cd-e3p.3)
- menu  - main menu / settings (new menu bead)
- diag  - on-device diagnostics (cd-89o.6)

Each mode is an object with tick(events) and render(); the loop asks the active one to handle the per-tick input events and draw. Chord events 'menu' and 'diag' (from cd-e3p.11) push/pop the corresponding mode over 'play'; the same chord (or CANCEL) returns to play. Entering menu/diag does NOT advance a game turn.

Deliver: a small mode stack / switch in engine.py (or a modes.py), the enter/exit wiring for the two chords, and a stub 'menu' and 'diag' mode so the switch is exercised before those screens are built out.
acceptance_criteria: engine main loop delegates tick+render to an active mode; 'diag' and 'menu' chords enter their modes and return to play without passing a turn; play state is untouched while a mode is up; stub modes prove the switch; documented in ENGINE.md.
notes:
Built. Chapter_7/game/modes.py (ModeStack + PlayMode + Menu/Diag stub overlays); engine.py Game slimmed to own InputModel + ModeStack + the ~20fps loop; ENGINE.md s4 + s2 updated. tests/test_modes.py = 10 off-device tests (world 12 / input 19 / modes 10 all green).

- ModeStack(base, {menu:.., diag:..}): base(play) always bottom, <=1 overlay on top. handle() consumes the 'menu'/'diag' chord events and toggles; everything else -> top.tick(); tick() -> 'exit' drops to base (stubs do this on CANCEL). render(screen) points screen.root_group at top.group, reassigns only on change.
- 'no game turn on mode switch' is structural: toggle event never reaches PlayMode.tick and play isn't ticked while an overlay is up. Tested.
- ModeStack imports nothing hardware-side (mode classes lazy-import displayio/util/world in __init__), so routing is unit-tested off-device.
- PlayMode absorbed the cd-e3p.2 Game scene (terrain grid + actor sprites + _sync/_render). PlayMode.tick still just advances the pulse - the turn loop is cd-e3p.3 (_resolve_turn still raises NotImplementedError).
- engine sets input.repeat_paused = stack.overlay_active() each tick.

Menu/Diag are _StubOverlay (centred label). cd-e3p.13 and cd-89o.6 replace them.

title: Button input model - presses, holds, and chords
description:
Chris flagged: the engine needs a logical button model layered above raw PicoSystem button reads, not ad-hoc polling in the turn loop.

PicoSystem controls: A, B, X, Y face buttons + d-pad (Up/Down/Left/Right).

The model must support:
- Single press - edge-triggered, one action per press.
- Press-and-hold - (maybe) auto-repeat for movement, and/or a distinct long-press action. Decide.
- Button PAIRS / chords - definitely needed: e.g. Up+X, A+B, and other pairs, as distinct actions. Decide press-vs-hold semantics for chords, the simultaneity window for 'pressed together', and how firing a chord suppresses the two individual-button actions.

One chord is reserved to enter diagnostic mode (see the diagnostic-mode bead).

Deliver an input module in Chapter_7/game/ that emits a documented event set consumed by the turn loop and menu/UI code, plus a doc of the full button map.
design:
SETTLED (turn model + Chris):
- Module input.py, pure (no displayio/board). InputModel.tick(buttons, now) -> list of events. buttons = hardware.read_buttons() 8-key dict; now = monotonic seconds. Off-device testable with synthetic (buttons, now) streams.
- NO long-press actions in v1. Hold matters only for the d-pad (auto-repeat). Face buttons fire once on press, inert until release.
- Events: MOVE_N/S/E/W, CONFIRM (a), CANCEL (b), AUX_X, AUX_Y, plus chord names from a binding table passed at construction. Module stays generic - it emits the bound NAME, doesn't know 'diag'/'menu' mean.
- Chords: simultaneous pairs only, edge-triggered, fire once per hold (release one to re-arm). Detection = both buttons down on the same poll. Reliability: any button that appears in some chord binding holds its single-press ONE tick (~50ms at 20fps); if the chord completes, chord fires and pending singles are cancelled; else the single fires next tick. Non-chord buttons fire immediately. All four face buttons are in a chord in v1, so all four take the 1-tick delay; d-pad never does.
- v1 chord bindings: {x,y} -> 'diag', {a,b} -> 'menu'. Table is extensible; turn-loop / UI beads add more.
- Auto-repeat: initial delay ~280ms, interval ~130ms (~7/s). These are INSTANCE config, not module constants, so the settings screen can retune them live. repeat_paused flag set by the engine each tick (from FOV / mode).
- Event queue: depth ~4, drop-oldest on overflow (stale turn-based input is worthless). Turn loop pulls one event per tick.

INPUT TRACE INSTRUMENTATION (Chris - for debugging input issues on-device):
- InputModel keeps a fixed ring buffer (~32) of short records: (t_ms, kind, detail) where kind in {press, release, repeat, chord, single-fired, single-cancelled}.
- snapshot() -> current held-button mask, per-held-button hold-duration ms, in-flight chord-candidate set, queue depth.
- Always recording from construction. cd-89o.6's input page renders trace + snapshot. Keep records tiny.

Button map + chord table -> a doc (doc/INPUT.md or ENGINE.md section).
acceptance_criteria: Input module in Chapter_7/game/ with a documented event enum/set; simultaneous-pair chord detection with a defined window + debounce; individual-button actions correctly suppressed when their chord fires; button-map + chord table written to a doc; unit-testable off-device (feed synthetic button states).
notes:
Built. Chapter_7/game/input.py + tests/test_input.py (19 tests, all pass) + doc/INPUT.md; ENGINE.md gets a new section 3 (later sections renumbered).

InputModel.tick(buttons, now) -> [events]; get() pops one/tick. Pure, off-device tested.
Events: MOVE_N/S/E/W (d-pad edge + auto-repeat), CONFIRM/CANCEL/AUX_X/AUX_Y (face, one per press, no long-press), chord names.
Chords: X+Y=diag, A+B=menu. Simultaneous pairs, once per hold, re-arm on release of a member. Chord-eligible buttons defer their single-press CHORD_WINDOW=50ms; if a member's single already fired this hold it can't join a chord ('hold A then press B' = CONFIRM+CANCEL, not menu).
repeat_delay/repeat_interval are instance attrs (settings-tunable, cd-e3p.13); repeat_paused set by engine (cd-e3p.3, FOV/mode). Queue bounded 4, drop-oldest.
Instrumentation: trace() (ring of 32 (t_ms,kind,detail)) + snapshot() (held, hold_ms, chord candidates/fired, queue depth) for the cd-89o.6 input page.

Not wired into engine.py — that's cd-e3p.12 (mode dispatch) + cd-e3p.3 (turn loop).
close_reason: Button input model built: game/input.py (pure, 19 off-device tests), doc/INPUT.md + ENGINE.md s3. Events MOVE_*/CONFIRM/CANCEL/AUX_X/AUX_Y + chords (X+Y=diag, A+B=menu). 50ms chord window, single-press suppression, bounded queue, trace()/snapshot() for cd-89o.6. Wiring into the loop is cd-e3p.12/.3.

title: Turn model
description: Strict player->monsters vs energy/speed system; what one d-pad press does; diagonal movement?
design:
Strict round-robin scheduling, equal speed in v1: turn = resolve player action -> each monster acts once (fixed list order) -> upkeep. Actor turn-taking goes through a Scheduler seam (actors_for_turn()) so an integer-speed or full energy/action-point scheduler can replace it later as a STRETCH GOAL without touching AI/combat/turn-loop.

Movement: 4-way only (N/S/E/W), Manhattan distance, 4-neighbour adjacency - FOV/AI-pathing/combat-reach all built on this. 8-way is a deliberate revisit gate (like ART.md s9 perspective) - decide before cd-e3p.4/.5/.6 are final. One press = one tile step = one turn. Held direction = cd-e3p.11 auto-repeats single steps, rate-capped, pauses while a monster is in view. No auto-travel in v1.

Turn-consuming: move, attack, wait, item use, stairs. Free (no turn): failed move into wall, inventory/map view, diagnostic toggle, look mode. A wait action passes exactly one turn.

Presentation: instant tile snaps in v1; apply_move() (logical) split from the draw step (presentation) so tile-to-tile slide animation can be added later. Slides stay strict - player slide in player sub-turn, each monster slide in its sub-turn, sequential. Batching visible actors' slides into one concurrent tween is an open sub-decision for the animation bead.

Main loop: non-blocking fixed tick ~15-20fps; a turn advances only on an actionable input event; between turns only the anim pulse advances. cycle pulse = presentation heartbeat, NOT the turn counter (turn count is its own int).
notes: Written up in Chapter_7/doc/ENGINE.md s1. Downstream: cd-e3p.2 (fork), cd-e3p.3 (turn loop), cd-e3p.11 (input model - held-repeat + monster-in-view pause + reserved chords), and the future animation bead (batched-slide sub-decision) all build against s1.
close_reason: Turn model decided with Chris and recorded in Chapter_7/doc/ENGINE.md s1. Strict/equal-speed with a scheduler seam for later energy system; 4-way movement (revisit gate); snap-now/slide-later presentation split; non-blocking ~15-20fps loop.

title: Document + script safe on-device serial diagnostics
description: This session repeatedly reinvented ad-hoc inline Python for reading a boards serial console (checking for a crash/traceback, soft-rebooting to capture one) with no write-up anywhere, despite doc/HARDWARE.md intro mentioning "raw-REPL scripting" was already used to probe this board back on 2026-09-04. Learned the hard way this session: (1) a passive read-only open (no writes) is always safe and never risks the I2C-wedge quirk; (2) a single Ctrl-D (0x04) soft-reboot to capture a fresh boot+traceback works reliably with a PLAIN os.open()+select()+read() loop; (3) setting the tty to raw mode via the tty/termios modules made it return nothing useful (unexplained, but reproduced twice) -- do not do that; (4) multiple quick resets back-to-back reliably wedges the shared I2C bus (doc/HARDWARE.md), needing a real USB unplug/replug to clear -- so a serial-check tool must never auto-retry/loop resets. Write Chapter_8/tools/serial_check.py (passive read by default, --reboot for one controlled soft-reboot capture, auto-detect the /dev/cu.usbmodem* port) and document the recipe + gotchas in a new Chapter_8/doc/SERIAL.md, cross-linked from doc/HARDWARE.md and doc/DEPLOY.md.
notes: Built Chapter_8/tools/serial_check.py (passive read by default, --reboot for one controlled soft-reboot capture, auto-detects /dev/cu.usbmodem*, flags a detected traceback or the I2C-wedge RuntimeError) and Chapter_8/doc/SERIAL.md (the recipe + gotchas), cross-linked from doc/HARDWARE.md and doc/DEPLOY.md. Immediately proved its worth in the same session: passive mode caught main.py had crashed to a 'Done' REPL state without needing a reset, and --reboot's single controlled soft-reboot captured the exact traceback (I2C wedge) that explained a screen that looked broken but wasn't a code bug.

title: Chapter 8 - Power management (no physical power switch)

title: DiagMode costs ~21.5KB to open — the RAM screen is the biggest allocation
description: Measured on-device 2026-09-04: opening DiagMode builds 14 bitmap_label lines at ~1.5KB each = ~21.5KB, lazily and kept. It's the single largest allocation on the board and it's pure observer-effect — you pay 21KB to look at the free number. 'ready free' is ~73KB so it's not a crash risk now, but it halves the visible margin the moment you diagnose, and deep in a run it's the riskiest open.
design:
Options (see doc/MEMORY-MAP.md sec5 item 2):
(a) One whole-page bitmap_label: ~9KB, but needs it CONTIGUOUS — the exact thing that OOM'd deep in a run and drove the 14-line split (cd-yl4). Viable again at 73KB ready IF built on first open with a MemoryError fallback to 'diag unavailable'. Best case ~12KB saved.
(b) label.Label for the static lines (board id / cpython ver / flash total) built once at open — label.Label's glyph-TileGrid churn only hurts on frequent .text= rewrites, and diag repaints are rare (every 4th render, on change only). Needs label.mpy back on the device (just removed in cd-dsc.6.2 — trivially re-added). Mixed: label.Label static + a few bitmap_label churny lines.
(c) Narrow _LINE_W 38 -> ~32 (longest real line is ~30 chars). ~15pct, ~3KB, zero risk.
(d) Fewer lines — _MAX_LINES 14, but several chord-stat lines could be one wrapped line.
Start with (c)+(d) (safe), measure, then decide on (a)/(b).
notes:
REPL measurement: 14x util.init_label(FONT, text=' '*38) = 21472 bytes, ~1533 ea. Setting a real (shorter) string on one FREED 2368 bytes — the ' '*38 _BLANK initial text is pessimal-wide; but fixed-width %-*s padding re-grows them on _repaint anyway.
Final: _MAX_LINES 14->12 (10 used). On-device 4x-averaged: real DiagMode = 12044 bytes/instance (was ~21472 as 14 line-labels). ~9.4KB saved on diag open. Deployed + verified rendering (.text correct, _page not None, repaint-after ~96 bytes).
close_reason: Done. One lazy fixed-geometry page bitmap_label replaces 14 line-labels. On-device: first repaint 13.3KB (was ~21.5KB), repaint-after ~0.1KB (bitmap reused), MemoryError-guarded. 171 tests pass. Deployed.

title: Tile sheet RAM footprint: right-size palettes, then merge 4 sheets to 1
description: The four tile .bmp sheets (terrain/heroes/creatures/objects) each ship a 256-entry palette table, so adafruit_imageload builds a ~2KB displayio.Palette per sheet — ~8KB total — for a shared 40-colour master palette (game/tiles/palette.json, capacity 64) and only 21 tiles across all four sheets. See doc/MEMORY-MAP.md sec5.
design:
Two steps, do in order:

STEP A (big win, low risk) - right-size the palette table.
tilelib.write_bmp() calls pal.flat_256() which pads to 256 RGB triples; PIL then writes biClrUsed=256 and imageload allocates displayio.Palette(256). Change to emit exactly len(pal.rgb) entries (40). Each on-device Palette drops ~2KB -> ~320B: saves ~6-7KB across the 4 sheets. NO change to tile indices, tiles.json, world.py/generator.py constants, util.py, or tests - just rebuild the 4 BMPs (tools/build_tiles.py) and redeploy. Verify: 157+ tests still pass, on-device 'ready free' up ~6KB, sprites render correct colours.

STEP B (smaller extra win, higher churn) - merge to one sheet.
All 21 tiles into one tiles.bmp (128x48, 3 rows @ 8 cols = 6144B vs 4x2048=8192B) with one Palette. Saves ~2KB bitmap + collapses 4 Palette objects to 1 (~1KB more) on top of A. Requires: global tile renumber 0..20; rewrite CORPSE_TILE/WALL_TILE/STAIRS_* in world.py and DIRT/FLAGSTONE/WALL/STAIRS_* in generator.py; drop or fix actor['sheet'] (modes._actor_sheets, world.make_actor, main._PLACEHOLDER_MOBS); update every test asserting a tile index or sheet name; regen tiles.json. Decide whether B's ~3KB is worth it after measuring A.
notes:
Prompted by the 2026-09-03 RAM writeup (doc/MEMORY-MAP.md). Related: OnDiskBitmap for the sheets (streams bitmap data from flash, ~6KB) is an alternative/additional lever noted on cd-dsc.6 - could stack with STEP A.
--- 2026-09-03: STEP A done (uncommitted) ---
tilelib.Palette.flat_256() -> flat_table(): emits exactly len(self.rgb)=40 RGB triples instead of padding to 256. tilelib.write_bmp() calls it.
Rebuilt the 4 sheets (tools/build_tiles.py): each .bmp 3126 -> 2262 bytes, biClrUsed 256 -> 40. RGBA output byte-identical (verified vs old terrain.bmp). tiles.json unchanged. doc/preview/* unchanged (contact sheets render from pal.rgb directly).
171 tests pass.
Expected on-device: displayio.Palette(40) not Palette(256) per sheet -> ~6-7KB heap back. NEEDS deploy + diag read to confirm 'ready free'.
STEP B (merge to 1 sheet) not started - pending Chris's call on whether ~3KB more is worth the tile-renumber churn.
--- 2026-09-04: STEP A confirmed on-device ---
Deployed + reset. Serial boot log (current tree, 48x48 + step A):
  Ch7 boot  free=122848   Ch7 level free=117728   Ch7 ready free=72880
REPL check: util.load_bitmap('terrain') -> len(pal)==40 (was 256); 2nd sheet load costs ~3.0KB (was ~5KB w/ Palette(256)). ~9KB back at 'ready' vs pre-step-A.
'ready free' history: ~48k (pre-48x48) -> ~64k (post-E, pre-A) -> ~73k (now).

OBSERVER EFFECT found while measuring: opening DiagMode allocates ~21.5KB (14 bitmap_label lines x ~1.5KB measured at REPL). That's the biggest single alloc on the board and it's the RAM screen itself. Spun to cd-dsc.6.3.

title: Corpses wake to hunt and trail the hero

- world.resolve_turn: snapshot the roster BEFORE _apply_player_action (turn order fixed at turn start -- ENGINE.md 1.1); also skip actor.get('corpse') and actor not in world.actors and dead-hero.

- test_combat.test_corpse_never_gets_a_turn_and_never_follows_the_hero (WANDER_CHANCE=1.0, 6 turns, assert never in the monster_turn list, didn't move, never got ai='hunt').

title: On-device diagnostic mode - RAM / flash / timing readout
description:
Once Ch7 runs on real PicoSystem hardware we hit issues (OOM, load failures, slow turns) where on-device data is the fastest path to a fix. This bead = the live stats readout page. The always-on diagnostic event-log ring buffer split out to cd-89o.10.

Entry: the X+Y chord (cd-e3p.11) toggles the diag overlay (cd-e3p.12). A cycles pages, B exits.

SYSTEM page surfaces:
- RAM: gc.mem_free() / gc.mem_alloc() sampled AFTER gc.collect() (raw mem_free under-reports); free_low low-water mark since boot; heap total. Sampled on a ~0.5Hz timer in the engine loop, not per-frame (collect costs ms).
- Flash: os.statvfs('/') free / total.
- Frame time ms (last + max).
- Board id + CircuitPython version.
- Actor count, turn count, depth.

INPUT page = the existing chord_stats/held/trace view (cd-e3p.14).

Keep it guardable so it costs ~nothing when not shown (text refresh every 3rd render only; RAM sampler is a cheap timestamp compare).
design:
Decisions:
- Overlay on top of game vs full replacement screen (overlay is more useful mid-bug, costs more render).
- Ring buffer size (16? 32?) and entry struct (bytes vs small tuples).
- Code table location - shared module so engine code can log without importing UI.
- Is the log always recording (from boot) or only after diagnostic mode first opened? (Always recording is the point - catch the bug before you knew to look.)
- Any way to dump the log over serial/USB for off-device capture.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic screen reachable via the reserved chord; shows RAM, flash, timing, seed, entity count, CP/board info; ring-buffer code log always recording from boot and displayed newest-first; documented code table; measured overhead when hidden is negligible (state it).
notes: Slice implemented 2026-08-30: game/metrics.py (pure) + DiagMode 2-page. Ring-buffer event log = cd-89o.10.

BOOT is normally just the bootloader-entry pin sampled at power-on, but on RP2350/CircuitPython it should also be readable as a plain GPIO during normal program execution (need to confirm which pin it's wired to and that CircuitPython doesn't reserve it). If it works as a general-purpose button, it's a second input alongside touch -- useful because touch-only has no way to say 'take an action independent of screen position,' e.g. explicitly toggling between ornament/ambient mode and interactive/game mode (relates to cd-ork's power-management work and cd-zw2.7's ornament mode) without relying on stillness-detection alone. Investigate: (1) which GPIO BOOT maps to and whether CircuitPython exposes it cleanly via board/microcontroller.Pin without conflicting with boot-select behavior, (2) debounce needs, (3) prototype a demo using it if it pans out.

title: Investigate real low-power/sleep options beyond backlight blanking
description: Before assuming 'blank the screen' meaningfully extends battery life, investigate what power this board's components (RP2350, GC9A01A display, CST816 touch, QMI8658 IMU) actually draw when idle-but-powered vs. what CircuitPython's alarm/sleep APIs could cut. Questions: does the RP2350 port support light/deep sleep in CircuitPython, and can it wake on touch (I2C interrupt line?) or only on a timer; what's the re-init cost/reliability of display+I2C peripherals after a real sleep vs. just leaving them powered with the backlight off; is it worth the complexity given the known I2C-bus-wedge quirk (doc/HARDWARE.md) that repeated resets can trigger. Research task -- outcome informs whether the other power-management beads under cd-ork target simple backlight blanking or something deeper.
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-13, written up in Chapter_8/doc/POWER.md. Bottom line: backlight-only blanking (cd-ork.1/.2) is the right stopping point. This board has no hardware path to wake specifically on touch via CircuitPython's alarm module (CST816 has no interrupt pin wired out, irq_pin=None) -- real sleep could only wake on a timer, which is less touch-responsive than the current always-awake+blanked-backlight approach. alarm module support itself is unconfirmed on this exact firmware build. Deep sleep's full-restart-on-wake risks the documented I2C-wedge pattern for an unsized power gain (no idle-current figures exist for CST816/QMI8658C to estimate payoff). Two cheap follow-ups filed: cd-ork.4 (confirm alarm module presence, P4) and a note on cd-bp3.6.1 (piggyback a rough current-draw measurement during the multimeter session).
close_reason: researched, written up in doc/POWER.md -- backlight-only blanking recommended, cheap follow-ups filed separately

title: Gameplay idea: non-combat NPCs (anti-hero / thief)
notes:
Design idea (Chris, 2026-09-01), NOT scheduled.

Non-combat / low-combat NPCs the hero occasionally runs into:
- ANTI-HERO: another adventurer. Not necessarily hostile. Might ignore the hero, say a line, or race for the same loot/stairs.
- THIEF: approaches, steals an item (from inventory -- cd-e3p.8) or gold, then flees toward the nearest exit; catch it to get the item back. Doesn't otherwise fight.
- Could also just be a talker: says something and runs away (flavour / hints / lore).

Shared seam with cd-bv3 (ghosts): needs an AI behaviour that is NOT 'step toward hero and attack' -- e.g. 'flee' (step AWAY from hero / toward an exit), 'idle+bark' (emit a log line, then wander), 'seek goal' (head for stairs or a loot tile, not the hero). ai.py currently has only sleep/hunt. Depends loosely on the message log (done) and inventory (cd-e3p.8) for the thief.

title: Gameplay idea: corpse re-animation
notes:
Design idea (Chris, 2026-09-01), NOT scheduled -- surfaced while fixing the corpse-follow bug (cd-add). The bug was corpses waking to 'hunt'; the accidental behavior suggested a real mechanic.

Some corpses re-animate a few turns after death:
- a fraction come back as MONSTERS (undead) -- fight the hero. Could be a weaker/reskinned version of what died, or a fixed 'zombie'/'skeleton'.
- a fraction come back as GHOSTS -- do NOT fight or interact with the hero, just drift / pass through walls / maybe emit a log line. Atmosphere, not threat.
- most stay dead.

Implementation seam already exists: corpses are actors with corpse=True that resolve_turn skips. Re-animation = an upkeep check that flips corpse=True off and sets ai/hp (monster) or a new non-combat 'ghost' ai mode. Ghost = a third ai behaviour alongside sleep/hunt (wander-ish, non-blocking, no _step_toward attack). Ties into cd-5j4 (non-combat NPC behaviour is the same new seam).

title: PicoSystem RGB status LED support
description:
The PicoSystem status LED is a 3-pin PWM RGB LED - board.LED_R/LED_G/LED_B = GPIO 14/13/15, active-low / common-anode (verify on device) - NOT a NeoPixel (no board.NEOPIXEL). hardware._picosystem() currently sets gd.neopixel = None and nothing drives the LED.

Add a uniform LED API to GameDisplay:
- set_led(r, g, b)  with 0-255 per channel; None-safe no-op on boards/desktop without an LED
- _picosystem(): back it with pwmio.PWMOut on the 3 pins (invert duty for active-low), no bundle lib needed
- _pybadge()/_clue()/etc: map set_led onto their existing NeoPixel (.fill), or leave as the no-op
- retire the ad-hoc gd.neopixel slot + main.py's 'if display.neopixel is not None: fill(...)' in favour of set_led

Use it for status cues: a boot heartbeat / 'ready' colour now; low-HP red, diagnostic-mode tint etc. later.
acceptance_criteria: GameDisplay.set_led(r,g,b) drives the PicoSystem LED via pwmio; a no-op (no error) on boards without an LED and on desktop; main.py shows a boot/ready colour through it; the gd.neopixel slot is gone; LED wiring noted in DEPLOY.md / hardware docs.
notes: From the cd-89o.8 prep - Chris confirmed the PicoSystem has no NeoPixel. A boot-colour cue would also help the smoke test (cd-89o.8): LED on = code reached run().

title: Split diagnostics: game/ core + on-demand diag/ modules
description:
Chris's idea (on the radar, not now): split diagnostics so heavy/optional diag code is copied to the device only when you want that aspect.

STRUCTURE
- Chapter_7/game/diag/   - a package, ALWAYS deployed. The core: the DiagMode shell + page registry, one built-in 'core' page (gc.mem_free, os.statvfs flash, turn/frame ms), and the sys.path bootstrap for the device's /diag dir.
- Chapter_7/diag/        - repo-side, individual optional page modules (input_timing.py, render_profiler.py, levelgen_inspect.py, fov_overlay.py, ...). NOT deployed by default.

ON DEVICE
- CIRCUITPY/game/diag/   - always present.
- CIRCUITPY/diag/        - empty/absent by default; drop an optional page .py here to enable it.

MECHANISM
- game/diag/ at init: if '/diag' exists, sys.path.append('/diag') (CircuitPython only auto-searches / and /lib, so a bare /diag dir needs this). Then for each optional page it knows about, try: import <name> except ImportError: skip. Present -> registered as a selectable DiagMode page; absent -> costs nothing.
- game/ code must NEVER hard-import an optional page - only game/diag/ does, guarded.
- Collection hooks that must always run stay in their home module (input.py trace()/snapshot()/chord_stats() already do); optional pages only READ those + render.
- tests/ adds Chapter_7/diag/ to sys.path so optional pages keep off-device tests.

Four deploy categories after this: doc/ (never), tools/ (never), game/ incl. game/diag/ (always), diag/ (on demand).

Needs a deploy story - a 'copy these for diag X' script or documented step - ties into cd-89o.1 (main.py) and cd-89o.2 (bring-up).

TRIGGER to actually do it: diag code starts costing real RAM/flash on device, or 3+ diag pages exist. Companion to cd-89o.6.
acceptance_criteria: game/diag/ package holds the DiagMode shell + core page + the /diag sys.path bootstrap; Chapter_7/diag/ has >=1 optional page module; DiagMode discovers optional pages by guarded import and degrades cleanly when /diag is empty or a module is absent; no game/ module hard-imports an optional page; a documented/scripted way to deploy a chosen page to CIRCUITPY/diag/; off-device tests cover the optional pages; ENGINE.md / a deploy doc updated.
notes: Radar item from the cd-e3p.14 session. Revisit with cd-89o.6 (full diag mode) - that's when the page count / RAM cost grows enough to justify the split.
